Publication figure specifications and export bundles

Source: vignettes/publication-figures.Rmd
publication-figures.Rmd

Shennong figures remain native ggplot, patchwork, or ComplexHeatmap objects. The publication engine attaches a lightweight specification instead of introducing a new plotting class, so ordinary + theme(...) composition keeps working.

Profiles and automatic sizing

Generic profiles describe screen, column, page, and slide constraints. They do not claim to replace current journal artwork instructions; verify those before submission.

library(Shennong)
library(Seurat)

sn_list_figure_profiles()

pbmc <- qs2::qs_read(pbmc_fixture)
pbmc <- sn_run_cluster(
  pbmc,
  normalization_method = "seurat",
  nfeatures = 1500,
  dims = 1:15,
  resolution = 0.6,
  species = "human",
  verbose = FALSE
)

plot <- sn_plot_dim(
  pbmc,
  reduction = "umap",
  group_by = "real_response",
  split_by = "real_batch",
  title = "Kotliarov PBMC response groups"
)

sn_recommend_figure_size(plot, profile = "double_column")
plot

The example above is rendered from 2,000 real CITE-seq cells and retains the study’s responder and acquisition-batch labels. Point size follows a clamped power rule, and high-density layers are recommended for rasterization while text and geometry remain vector in PDF/SVG output.

Inspect and apply a specification

Core Shennong plots attach shennong_figure_spec automatically. Any native plot can also be profiled after construction.

plot <- sn_apply_figure_profile(plot, "double_column")
sn_get_figure_spec(plot)$recommended
sn_validate_figure(plot)
plot

Validation reports calculated dimensions, text and raster settings, small panels, category/legend overload, long labels, pagination, extreme aspect ratios, and dense networks. It predicts likely problems; final visual review is still required.

Deterministic export

sn_save_figure() supports PDF, SVG, TIFF, and PNG without depending on the current RStudio graphics device. PDF uses base R’s portable device. SVG uses the optional svglite package rather than a platform-specific X11/Cairo device; when it is unavailable, Shennong stops before drawing with an actionable dependency message. Explicit dimensions override automatic values.

figure_dir <- file.path(tempdir(), "shennong-real-figures")
dir.create(figure_dir, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)

png_path <- sn_save_figure(
  plot,
  file.path(figure_dir, "kotliarov_response.png"),
  profile = "double_column"
)

pdf_path <- sn_export_figure(
  plot,
  file.path(figure_dir, "kotliarov_response.pdf"),
  profile = "double_column"
)

file.info(c(png_path, pdf_path))[, c("size", "mtime")]

For a reproducible handoff, export the rendering, source table, calculated specification, session information, checksums, and validation result together.

manifest <- sn_export_figure_bundle(
  plot,
  path = file.path(figure_dir, "kotliarov_response_bundle"),
  formats = c("pdf", "png"),
  include_data = TRUE,
  include_spec = TRUE,
  include_session = TRUE,
  profile = "single_column"
)
manifest$files
manifest$validation$status

Result-aware sn_plot_de(), sn_plot_enrichment(), and sn_plot_gsea() attach their standardized plotting tables as bundle source data. The QC, clustering, integration, annotation projection, bulk, dimensional, feature, dot, heatmap, violin, box, bar, composition, and Milo helpers also expose figure metadata for automatic sizing and QA.
